content:
aisha: Quick RFC follow-up — need a decision on backfill vs prewarm priority when dedicated pools hit burst.

mike: Proposal A = strict SLO-first; prewarm tokens used by high-SLO tenants, backfill is best-effort. Keeps latency stable.

sophia: Concern: that blows estimated monthly cost +35% in our sim for small teams. prewarm credits get hoarded.

ben: Proposal B = proportional prewarm: allocate prewarm proportional to committed headroom, leftover goes to backfill.

grant: How do we order evictions? LRU on idle)? Also do we let backfill preempt prewarm if queue spikes?

mike: Eviction order: (1) ephemeral backfill, (2) burst-soft reservations, (3) prewarm tokens — unless tenant has emergency SLA flag.

sophia: Simulation snippet we ran:
```
workload: 500 tenants
prewarm-config: proportional
metrics: p99 latency stable, cost +18%
edge-case: burst x2 causes 12% request failrate for backfill
```

aisha: We need a policy that's simple to explain to sales + predictable billing for finance.

ben: My fav: start with proportional prewarm + a small 'grace' bucket for preemption. If it fails, fallback to strict SLO route.

grant: Agree. Also add an audit log for each eviction + reason (billing_id, SLO_tag)

mike: Draft DSL for operator-config (WIP):
```
pool_policy {
  prewarm_strategy: proportional
  prewarm_ratio: 0.6
  grace_bucket_tokens: 100
  eviction_order: [backfill, burst_soft, prewarm]
}
```

aisha: Action items: mike -> finish DSL + add metrics (cost delta + p99). sophia -> run sim with production traces. ben -> add audit log design. grant -> billing wording for docs.

deploy-bot: canary: policy=v0.3-proportional rolled to staging at 16:42 UTC :rocket:

mike: I'll open a short RFC PR with the DSL and sim results by EOD.

sophia: :eyes: will run sims overnight and post results.

ben: :thumbsup:

aisha: thanks all — sync tomorrow 9am PT if anything blocks.
